reviews.finding: The cited passage directly supports BERT outperforming CRF and spaCy in MEDDOCAN detection/classification due to recall. It does not give numeric performance; broader task coverage is not established by this citation.
reviews.gap_review: Numeric limitations are stated; duplicated gaps and unread-ID bookkeeping remain.

answer.text: BERT outperforms CRF and spaCy classifiers in the MEDDOCAN detection and classification scenarios, primarily due to greater recall.
answer.heading: Answer

reviews.finding: Three cited passages support random language groups of two or three, minibatch language alternation, no source-language input to the auxiliary decoder, multilingual/multi-task training then monolingual finetuning, and a five-model ensemble.
reviews.gap_review: The reported gap that the seven languages are not enumerated is misleading: the read passage gives five languages (de,en,fr,ru,sv) and the other two (es,fi), which covers all seven.

answer.text: Multilingual training is performed by randomly alternating between languages for every new minibatch, using random groupings of two to three languages. No source language information is passed to the auxiliary decoder. The approach is paired with multi-task learning and monolingual finetuning, using an ensemble of five best models for final predictions.
answer.heading: Answer

reviews.finding: The cited passages describe previous FgNER methods and their architectures. They do not establish that all five listed systems were used as actual experimental comparators. Research should read the experiment/baseline section before making this stronger claim.
reviews.gap_review: Table/number limitations are acknowledged, but that does not supply support for the claimed comparator list.

answer.text: The authors compare their model with prior fine-grained NER systems including Ling et al. (linear perceptron), Yosef et al. (binary SVMs), Gillick et al. (context-dependent heuristics), Yogatama et al. (embedding-based), and Shimaoka et al. (attentive neural network with LSTMs).
